open_questions: Construction cost and Visa's lease term and rent: not disclosed in anything read (Bisnow gave no term).
Vertical construction start date: SF YIMBY says early summer 2021; the Port's December 2021 update says the site was 'approximately one year into' Phase 1 construction. No groundbreaking date found.
LEED: only a 2021 'aiming for Gold'; no certification record found.

Address: the repo's status.csv also gives Visa's address as 1051 3rd St, an address that two Building B sources (Mitsui Fudosan press release, CommercialSearch listing) attach to Building B instead. Flagged in the PR.
The Fieldwork opening date rests on a search excerpt of a July 28, 2026 press release that returned 403 here.

Images: no 'before' photo is hosted (until 2020 the parcel was the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot) and no rendering is hosted because the architects' renderings are not openly licensed; they are reachable through the architect sources listed here.

record.notes: Building G -- Visa Global/North America HQ, 13-story ~299,600 sf (283,320 office + 16,280 retail); Henning Larsen design, LEED Gold target; TCO Jan 2023, Visa occupancy Apr 2024, up to 1,500 employees (Port memo, Oct 2023; henninglarsen.com/projects/mission-rock-building-g). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row joined blklot 8719005, addressed to a compact office tower at the south end of block 8719 near the 3rd St/China Basin Channel bridge -- that tower is actually the pre-existing (1922/1991) Wharfside/Berry Building office campus at 185 Berry St ('China Basin Landing'), wholly unrelated to Mission Rock; the earlier join was a mistaken shape/position match, not verified against the real cross-street. Re-identified via a direct search confirming Visa's real address (1051 3rd St) sits at the cross-street Toni Stone Crossing -- a real, Mission-Rock-internal street -- and blklot 8719A008 is the one addressed '300 Toni Stone Xing' in DataSF's Assessor roll, positioned correctly at the north end of the site immediately next to Verde/China Basin Park (not the south end). Its ~53,000 sqft footprint is plausible for a tower-plus-podium base of this size.
